# Page 17^page=17
A simple assembly problem components Phone A Score A Phone B Score BObjective: Maximize the overall score

# Page 18^page=18
Solution Are you sure that the solution that you found is the best one? How can you certify it? How much are you willing to spend to have one more display, or keyboard, or memory board? Is it worth introducing a completely new product?

# Page 19^page=19
How OR approaches the problem Decisions What decisions did you take? How do you characterize your solution? Rules How do you combine components to obtain a product? Objective What do you have to optimize?

# Page 20^page=20
Decisions = variables xA = how many phones of type A xB = how many phones of type B

# Page 21^page=21
Rules = Constraints The number of used components cannot exceed the available ones 1xA +2xB ≤ 10 display 2xA +2xB ≤ 18 memory 1xA +3xB ≤ 12 transmission 2xA +3xB ≤ 21 keyboard 1xA ≤ 9 navigation 1xA ≤ 10 camera xA,xB ≥ 0 non negativity

# Page 22^page=22
Objective function Maximize the overall score max 3xA +8xB

# Page 23^page=23
One simple solution method Exploit the fact that we have only 2 variables Give a geometric representation xA xB 5 1xA +2xB ≤ 10 10 9 9 2xA +2xB ≤ 18 4 12 xA +3xB ≤ 12 7 2xA +3xB ≤ 21 xA ≤ 9 xA ≤ 10 Feasible region inﬁnite number of solutions “Interesting” solutions xA =0,xB =4 v =32 xA =6,xB =2 v =34 xA =8,xB =1 v =32 xA =9,xB =0 v =27

# Page 24^page=24
Skills of an OR expert Analyze the problem Knowledge of the application ﬁeld Communication skills to understand and explain Knowledge of the OR methods Ability in building mathematical models Interpret the results Search on the internet information about the job of operations research

# Page 25^page=25
Program of the course Introduction to OR Optimization problems and their formulations; decision variables, objective function, constraints. Modeling techniques Graphs and net work ﬂows problems Trees and graphs. Shortest paths, maximum ﬂow, minimum cost ﬂow, assignments. Some data structures and solution algorithms. Complexity analysis Linear Programming Geometry of Linear Programming, vertices and basic solutions. Duality theory, complementary slackness, the simplex method; geometrical and economical interpretation. Basic solutions and optimality conditions. Integer Linear Programming and combinatorial optimization Cutting planes methods. Relaxations and branch and bound algorithm. Computational complexity and Heuristic algorithms Basics of computational complexity. Greedy and local search. Applications of OR in computer science and telecommunications: Routing, scheduling, location, transportation.

# Page 26^page=26
Metacognitive ﬂows: map of our trip Through mathematical modeling and quantitative reasoning, learners can cope with optimization problems. Learners can create eﬃcient solution methods for optimization problems arising in real life or in their professional environment. modeling optimization problems graphs and networks linear programming integer linear programming basic heuristic algorithms Algorithmic aspects Modeling techniques Geometric interpretation Optimality conditions

Exam Written exam : 23 points: part 1 (13) closed book (!): standard exercises part 2 (10) open book: creative exercises lab exam: 4 points, separate event, one per session Bonus points (max 3 + 2) will complete the 4 missing points for those who could not attend the activities there will be an additional question in the ﬁrst part (4 points) Lab mini projects: in groups skip the lab exam Sufﬁciency: >17.5 in the written exam + lab exam
